result.summary: Moves fee estimator shutdown flushing and unregistration to occur after queued background validation callbacks are drained. This ensures any pending block updates are processed by the estimator before its state is written to disk, preventing saved fee statistics from falling behind the active chain tip.
result.problem: During node shutdown, fee estimator stats were flushed and unregistered before background validation callbacks drained. If a block update remained queued, the fee estimator missed it and saved a tip height older than the chain tip; on restart, the mempool fee estimator ignores its saved file when the tips do not match.
evidence: PR description: 'The mempool estimator added in #34075 persists mined-block stats for restart... A queued block update can leave the saved stats behind the active chain tip, so the mempool estimator ignores its file on restart.'
Commit 08729e6ef9 adds a unit test verifying that without the fix, block updates queued after scheduler shutdown are excluded from persisted fee estimates.
result.card: Reorders node shutdown so that fee estimator state is saved and unregistered after queued background validation callbacks are drained. Previously, pending block updates could be missed during shutdown, causing saved fee estimator state to lag behind the chain tip and leading the mempool fee estimator to discard the cached estimates file upon restart. The PR includes a unit test in node_init_tests that reproduces and verifies the callback drain ordering.

risk.why: A flaw in shutdown reordering could cause crashes or deadlocks during shutdown if callbacks interact unexpectedly with the estimator.
